title: Deep derived pure braids need not be 1-solvable
scope: Full current four-page manuscript, all necessary central mathematical support and primary interfaces, independent proof reconstruction, fresh exact controls and current published finite replay.
strongest_verified_claim: For every m>=3 and finite integer k>=1, P_m^(k) contains a classical disk pure braid whose standard oriented closure is not integrally smoothly 1-solvable in Otto Definition 2.3. Hence P_m^(n+2) is not contained in F_n^m for every integer n>=1. The specified depth-three commutator has reduced Artin length104 and signature-2.
claims_checked: Signature homogenization bound and nonhomomorphism on P3
Pointwise -1 signature vanishing for the exact integral smooth 1-solution definition
Finite-derived-depth quasimorphism persistence through solvable/amenable quotients
Power amplification, linking numbers, split-strand extension and filtration inclusion
Explicit P3 third-derived membership and complete finite numerical certificate
limitations: Finite k; witnesses may depend on k; no intersection witness.
m>=3 and ordinary derived series only; no rational, surface-braid, lower-central or power-subgroup extension.
104 is the exhibited reduced word/diagram length, not a minimum crossing number.
The explicit finite example is depth3; all-depth conclusion is proved analytically, not by extrapolation.
No priority/continued-openness determination, independent human or journal review, or formal proof-assistant certification.
Current replay does not rerun archived historical SymPy recovery/full transport suites.
